title: Diabetic foot infection

items: A diabetic foot infection is an infection of the foot in someone with diabetes, often starting from a sore or ulcer.
It can spread to deeper tissues and bone.
Redness, warmth, swelling, pain, or pus from a foot sore.
Culture of deep tissue or bone, rather than a surface swab alone.
X-ray of the foot, and MRI if bone infection is suspected.
Blood sugar control (HbA1c) and blood flow tests (ABI or Doppler).
Your team will decide on antibiotics, wound care, and whether surgery is needed.
Good control of blood sugar helps healing.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Check your feet every day, and wear proper footwear.
Do not walk barefoot, and tell your team about any new sore.
Attend all foot reviews, and keep your diabetes appointments.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Spreading redness, a foot that is dark, or a bad smell from the wound
Severe pain or a foot that feels cold or numb
